coverage.assessment: Julius's account loses three causal links: why his father objected, why Julius came to England, and why he is going to Paris. Carter's forced-pace warning also loses its rationale. The photograph setup and the 'this morning' visit are intact.

In Tuppence's complaint, 'they send us a green one' has no antecedent once the Government is cut. Carter's farewell and the handshake are gone, so the exit is abrupt. The lunch is no longer placed in the restaurant, which is harmless.

'When did you last see your cousin?' is now unattributed and follows Julius directly, so the asker is unclear. Tommy's merged lunch/Hersheimmer/taxi speech flattens the shared-thought beat. Other attributions are clear.

Carter's 'needn't be cast down if you fail' and his hope that the pace will be forced are cut, so the warning becomes unhedged. The salary, the 'this morning' visit, Paris tomorrow, the only copy and the unnamed real name are all correct.

The cliffhanger ends on 'Quiet, unassuming sort of chap.' Nothing from Chapter VII's confirmation is imported, Julius's account carries no added doubt, and there is no hint about the photograph's real location.

Julius's American colour is thinned: the Piccadilly policeman, 'a mite hasty' and 'London gets my goat' are gone. The narrator's ironic 'They bowed before it' is also lost. The leads' banter and Carter's monotone are largely kept.
The coincidence/luck theme, Tuppence's money creed and the nondescript-Brown echo all survive. The losses are of execution rather than of thematic structure.
Dependencies 0–2 are intact at both endpoints. For dependency 3, the local endpoint survives, but the partner draft 027 has cut 'went out West… her photograph'.

strengths: The closing sting keeps its rhythm, from Tuppence's 'unformulated dread' to the stammered question and Julius's 'Yes, I do. No, I don't. Half a second.', ending on the unassuming-Brown line.
The real-name whisper, 'he's IT!', the steel image, the pinch and 'We've got a job!' all survive in order.
The blackmail exchange keeps Tuppence's dark 'I'm not sure I have,' as the payoff.
'Another man this time' preserves the two-visitor logic that makes the cliffhanger work.
summary: The revision keeps the required plot spine: the luck/fate theme, Carter's terms and disclaimer, three hundred a year, the unnamed real name, the 'steel' image, the blackmail joke, Julius's age and genealogy, the Sicily line, the 'this morning' visitor, Paris tomorrow, the only-copy photograph and the Inspector Brown sting. All eight verbatim passages survive. Most defects are revision-introduced over-compressions of material the first draft had kept. Carter's warning loses its hopeful and consoling hedges. Tuppence's form complaint loses its object, so 'they' has no antecedent. Julius's history loses three causal links. One question loses its speaker. Several voice touches are thinned. None of these is a blocker, but a few small restorations would repair them.
